Breeding trials, from line to recommendation

The corrected seven synthetic UC4 files the SME sent on 30 Sep 2026: which lines, where they were tested, what each plot measured, what the recommendation says, the rule that reproduces it, and whether the evidence traces back.

Inferred, not supplied. The recommendation file states outcomes and a rule version, not thresholds. The cut-points on this page are the simplest fixed values that reproduce every outcome. Confirm them with the UC4 expert before presenting them as the rule. Earlier profiles are kept in v2/report_v2.html (29 Sep) and v1/report_v1.html (kickoff).

Start here · plain language

What is in this data?

This is a synthetic snapshot, not results from live breeding systems. A line is a candidate plant material; a trial tests a group of lines at one site. The supplied PASS / HOLD / FAIL label describes a trial; each line now also carries its own advancement decision.

  • What we have. Seven files describe 150 lines, 72 trials, 720 plot values, 150 genomic records, 360 lab results and 216 field operations. Each trial has one of 7 PASS, 35 HOLD or 30 FAIL recommendations. Explore the sources.
  • What changed on 30 Sep. The SME re-linked lines, trials, plots and operations, and added pedigree, breeding stage, line decisions and per-plot measurements. Two files (genomics and recommendations) were resent unchanged from 29 Sep, so they do not connect by key to the rest. See what changed.
  • What a verdict means. SYN-TR-0003 is PASS (yield 10.79 t/ha, disease 3.3); SYN-TR-0037 is HOLD despite favourable wording. Its trial record reports 30% resistant materials, below the reconstructed PASS target; this share does not reconcile to the linked lines. SYN-TR-0001 is FAIL with disease 7.7. The cut-points used to explain these labels are inferred from the outcomes, not a supplied scoring policy. See the rule.
  • What we cannot conclude. A trial's yield or disease value is not the average of its own plots, its genomic summary does not match its lines, and a line's advancement decision does not follow its trials' verdicts. Until the SME explains how these relate, a trial verdict cannot justify a line decision. Review the evidence limits.
For technical readers · evidence audit

What can be joined, reproduced and trusted?

The counts below are checks on the supplied synthetic records. A reconstructed rule matching the records does not establish the SME's intended thresholds or make the underlying joins valid.

  • Joins. 11/14 recorded links resolve fully. The genomics and recommendations files keep their v2 keys: genomics lines resolve 0/150, recommendation trial GUIDs 0/72. This profile repairs them for analysis: recommendations by TRIAL_ID, a shared key (72/72), and genomics by the last GUID block, which is positional and not a verified join. 16/150 lines have no lab result. Link rates and their table.
  • Grain and provenance. The 720 plot values carry trait, unit, date, replicate and quality flag, and link trial and line. Lab results are dated and join lines, but have no trial key, trait dictionary or units. Plot values; lab detail.
  • Rule fit is not rule authority. A fixed-threshold reconstruction agrees with 72/72 supplied trial verdicts. 4/11 rationales stating all four named criteria are met still have a HOLD verdict: resistant-material share is omitted from the text. Inspect the observed threshold brackets and their source table.
  • Trial values do not trace back. 354/360 trial × trait pairs differ from the trial's plot mean. Trial GBV differs from the observed lines in 71/72 trials; resistant share in 59/72. 187/216 operation trial-line pairs lack a plot record. See reconciliation, plot-level and genomic results.
  • Status and dates. 47/72 trials with a verdict are not COMPLETE. Plot values are outside their trial's start year in 0/720 cases, operations in 148/216. ADVANCE lines are 23% of PASS-trial lines and 23% of FAIL-trial lines. Review all consistency checks and their denominators.

Questions for the UC4 expert: Can genomics and trial recommendations be regenerated from the corrected lines and trials? How are trial values computed from plots (which quality flags, which replicates)? How does a line's advancement decision relate to its trials' verdicts? What are the authoritative cut-points? What do the four lab traits and the operation quantity units mean? Is the intended crop maize? Until confirmed, none of these assumptions is a source fact.

Key findings

  • Two files were resent unchanged. genomics and recommendations are identical to the v2 files, so they still carry v2 keys. The other five were regenerated and share no GUID with v2. Genomics lines resolve 0/150 and recommendation trial GUIDs 0/72; 11 of 14 recorded links resolve fully.
  • The inferred rule still reproduces every verdict (72 of 72), as it must with an unchanged file: PASS 7, HOLD 35, FAIL 30. FAIL if yield < 7 t/ha or disease > 7; PASS if yield ≥ 9, moisture ≤ 22%, disease ≤ 5, GBV mean ≥ ~102 and resistant materials ≥ 50%; otherwise HOLD.
  • The rationale text hides one criterion. 4 of 11 trials whose rationale says all four criteria are met are HOLD, held back by the resistant-material share the text never mentions.
  • Plots now carry values, but not the trials' values. 354/360 trial × trait pairs differ from the mean of the trial's own plots, with or without non-accepted plots. The trial values were computed before these plots existed.
  • Genomic aggregates do not follow the observed lines either. The GBV mean differs from the lines observed in the trial in 71/72 trials (joined by GUID position). The v2 block-of-10 mapping now reproduces 0.
  • Lines carry their own decision again. Pedigree, breeding stage and ADVANCEMENT_DECISION are back (ADVANCE 35, HOLD 58, DISCARD 57). ADVANCE lines make up 23% of lines in PASS trials and 23% in FAIL trials: the line decision does not follow the trial verdict.
  • Trial status contradicts the verdicts. 47/72 trials with a verdict are not COMPLETE in the trial file, and 330/720 plot values sit on trials still PLANNED.
  • Plots follow the calendar; operations do not. 0/720 plot values fall outside their trial's start year, against 148/216 operations (dated April 2024 to October 2026). Only 46 of 72 trials have a planting operation to anchor a season, and 6 read in a plausible order.

Which recorded links resolve

Plant lifecycle

A season, phase by phase

To say what happened and when, every value is placed on the crop's season: before sowing, planting, vegetative growth, flowering, grain fill, harvest and the decision. The files never name the crop; the trait ranges fit maize, so maize stage codes are used. Each trial's season is counted in days from its first planting operation, and flowering is placed at planting + FLOWERING_DAYS. Plot observations and BEGIN_DATE are dated too; the consistency checks test them against the trial year.

46 of 72 trials can be placed on a season. 16 have both a planting and a harvest, and 6 of those are harvested after expected flowering. The rest are described without dates, and the assistant should say so rather than infer them.

What the assistant can say, one trial per verdict

Generated from the timeline table; every trial has one in tables/trial_timeline.csv.

  • SYN-TR-0033 (2026 trial, operations dated in another year ⚠): planted 10 Jun 2024; no irrigation recorded; flowering expected ~day 58 (07 Aug 2024); harvested 03 Sep 2026 (day 815). Verdict PASS: meets all five criteria.
  • SYN-TR-0060 (2026 trial, operations dated in another year ⚠): planted 20 Oct 2024; no irrigation recorded; flowering expected ~day 53 (12 Dec 2024); harvested 02 Jun 2025 (day 225). Verdict HOLD: misses the GBV target, resistant-material share.
  • SYN-TR-0001 (2024 trial, operations dated in another year ⚠): planted 18 Sep 2024; no irrigation recorded; flowering expected ~day 59 (16 Nov 2024); harvested 21 Jun 2025 (day 276). Verdict FAIL: disease score above 7.

Scoring

The trial recommendation and its rule

Each of the 72 trials carries a PASS, HOLD or FAIL, the trial-level values behind it and a rationale naming four criteria. Two knockouts (low yield, high disease) decide FAIL; five criteria together decide PASS. The cut-points are inferred: the file brackets them but does not state them.

Sources

Plot observations

New in v3: every observation row is one plot value for one of five field traits, with a unit, a date, a replicate and a quality flag. These are the first line-level field measurements in any UC4 archive.

Sources

Genomics

One genotyped sample per line with four marker calls, a genomic breeding value and QC. The file is unchanged from v2, so it joins the regenerated lines only by the last block of the GUID. The trial file summarises these values per trial.

Sources

Do the trial values trace back to plots and lines?

A breeder asking why a trial failed will want the plots and lines behind it. Neither the field values nor the genomic summaries can be rebuilt from the records the files link to the trial. The recommendation file is unchanged from v2, so it was computed before these plots and links existed.

Sources

Lab tests

Lab results attach to a line, not a trial. They are now dated, but some lines have none, trait names and units are missing, and the recommendation does not use them.

Sources

Field operations

Planting, fertiliser, irrigation, inspection and harvest, now with a quantity. The quantity units vary within an operation type, and the dates do not follow the trials they belong to.

Scoring

How tightly the data pins each cut-point

Each threshold lies somewhere in its bracket: the lower bound is the value closest to the line on one side, the upper bound on the other. used is the value this profile applies. Plant height, days to flowering and genomics QC never change an outcome.

Validation

Consistency checks

Operation rules test the record against the trial calendar and the extract (28 Nov 2026 02:43). Link and recommendation rules test whether trial-level values trace back to the lines the files connect to the trial. For the demo, the assistant should surface these as reasons for amber, not hide them.
